name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network activity on social platforms, including the CLSB methodology, CooRnet, and the ongoing VERA-AI Alert monitoring system. This is the researcher's signature methodological contribution and remains central to current work.

name: Information Disorder & Disinformation
description: Study of misinformation, disinformation and hybrid media manipulation dynamics, including narrative propagation, fact-checking support tools, and the conceptual foundations (fake news taxonomies) underpinning the researcher's broader agenda.

name: Platform Data Governance & Research Access
description: Research on social media APIs, data access regimes, and platform accountability under the EU Digital Service Act, including work on Meta datasets (CrowdTangle, URL Shares Dataset), the JRC/ECAT expert role on systemic risk of VLOPs, and the effects of Meta's political content policies.

name: Political Polarization & Italian Election Coverage
description: Long-running empirical program (MINE) mapping Italian news media and social media dynamics around national elections, partisan attention, insularity and cross-partisan engagement, and political parallelism, extending to comparative work in Brazil and Latin America.

name: Generative AI & LLMs in Content Analysis
description: Methodological research on integrating large language models and embedding models into social media content classification and political discourse analysis, including validation challenges of LLM-in-the-loop pipelines and teaching (IA Generativa e Media course).

name: Synthetic Media & Generative Manipulation
description: Emerging focus on how generative AI is used to produce deceptive visual and textual content in coordinated influence operations, such as AI-generated gambling promotion and deceptive information operations ('Zombie Internet').

name: Health Misinformation Networks
description: Cross-national studies (India, Nigeria, Italy) of coordinated networks and alternative influence networks circulating problematic health information, including COVID-19 fact-checking acceleration research.

name: Social TV & Second-Screen Engagement
description: Earlier but foundational research strand analyzing Twitter-based audience participation around television broadcasts, political talk shows and media events, establishing the researcher's early computational social media methods.

name: Sociocybernetics & Social Systems Theory
description: Theoretical grounding in Luhmannian social systems theory and sociocybernetics applied to internet studies, informing the researcher's broader epistemological approach to digital social phenomena.

name: MINE — Mapping Italian News Program
description: The institutional umbrella research program coordinating studies of Italian media coverage, social media's impact on elections, public opinion and health information; the stable organizing structure for most of the researcher's funded sub-projects since 2017.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.
